_readme: R347 Lane A — the intentional-layering allowlist (≤10 entries). Law: an entry exists ONLY for provably intentional layering (a written reason each); anything that merely 'looks fine' or hides a defect is refused. The detector (scripts/qa/overlap.mjs) filters ONLY big-fixed findings whose element selector starts with an entry's match; text-on-text, fixed-over-text, clipped and overflow findings are never allowlisted. Entries are added by the lane that proves the case, never to recover a red run.

entries.reason: R313 D9 / R315 K-A4 — the page's own drafting frame: four 1px hairlines at the 7px viewport inset, aria-hidden, pointer-transparent (styles/shell/sheet-frame.css). It intersects ~95% of the viewport BY DESIGN (it is the border, not a cover) and paints no ink except the hairlines; the reference's own page frame is the same construction. Proven intentional: its 4 borders are the only children, border 1px, background transparent.

R347 D6 (Lane B + Z, merged reasons) — the journey map's STICKY WINDOW at ≤991: the plan column is its own scroll track (Heron's own mobile architecture — the map pins while the closing column scrolls past). It owns its full-width grid track, contains only its own children (statement band, plan window, findings card — all in flow after the R347 re-seat, zero text-under-window findings), and never paints over neighbouring content (the r312 e2e invariant sweep asserts the closing column is never covered). Proven intentional: position sticky inside .jt-map-col, the section's own track ladder; the reference's own 51% walkthrough is a pinned map — deleting the pin would delete the section.

R353 P1 — the app shell's own fixed topbar (the AppShell contract from R353 P4: one header height token, the primary navigation). On a 390x844 viewport the 56-64px bar measures ~7% of the viewport area — over the 6% big-fixed threshold by construction, not by defect: it is the platform's global chrome, contains only its own controls, and the R353 P4 layout contract pins its z-index and height. Proven intentional: every authed page renders inside AppShell with the topbar; content scrolls under it by design.

R353 P1 — the auth/colleges/app sheets' own DRAFTING FRAME (patterns.css .auth-frame/.nf-frame, W7 dedup family of div.sheet-frame): four 1px hairlines at the 7px viewport inset, aria-hidden, pointer-transparent, decorative registration chrome present at every breakpoint by design. It intersects ~95% of the viewport BY CONSTRUCTION (it is the border, not a cover) — same proven-intentional case as the allowlisted div.sheet-frame.

R353 P1 — the 404/legal sheets' DRAFTING FRAME, the .auth-frame twin (patterns.css:635, W7 dedup — identical bodies, same layer). Decorative 1px fixed frame, aria-hidden, pointer-transparent; the big-fixed flag measures its inset box, not any ink. Same construction as div.sheet-frame / div.auth-frame.

R353 P1 — the AppShell's COLLAPSED sidebar rail (the same global chrome family as the allowlisted header.topbar): the icon-only navigation rail the app pins on content-width viewports by design. Its ~56-64px width measures >6% of a 360-640 viewport by construction, not by defect — it is the platform's primary navigation (the R353 P4 AppShell contract), contains only its own controls, and content scrolls beside it, never under its ink. Proven intentional: every authed page renders inside AppShell; the expanded drawer variant is the same nav at larger size.

R353 P1 — the patterns FilterBar's DOCUMENTED sticky mode (FilterBar.tsx:10-12 'pins it to the top of the app's scroll container', patterns.css:340 'a SOLID paper band + hairline — filters stay readable while rows slide beneath them'): the page's own filter controls, opaque background var(--bg) (occlusion-safe — content under it is genuinely hidden, the probe's coveredBy honors it), z-index 3 inside the scroll container. The >6% viewport fraction at 360x640 (17.4%) is construction (wrapped filter controls on a small viewport), not a defect — the same sticky-toolbars pattern as the allowlisted header.topbar.

R353 P1 — the patterns SplitView's sticky DETAIL pane (patterns.css:265, the R353 P4 dvh contract seat): the master-detail layout's right column sticks while the left list scrolls — a grid SIBLING track (grid-template-columns: minmax(320px,420px) + 1fr), so it never paints over the list, it owns its own track; hidden below 920px by design. The >6% viewport fraction at 1024/1440 (12.6-13.9%) is construction (a wide detail column on a 768px-tall viewport), not a cover — the same master-detail sticky pattern as div.jt-map-in (allowlisted R347 D6).

R356 Lane 2c — the people page's STICKY SAVE TOOLBAR (profile-data.css:251, role=toolbar, R349's own design): the field/file editor's save+cancel actions pin to the scroll container's bottom while the form scrolls above — the same sticky-action-bar pattern as the allowlisted div.pf-filterbar.sticky (page's own controls, opaque background, z-index inside the scroll container, FAB-lane-aware padding-inline-end 76px per its own R349-P5 fix). First surfaced by the param-route fixtures (the /admin/people/:id crawl — the populated editor layout was never crawlable before); its 60px bar measures 6.4-8.3% of 360-390px viewports by construction, not by defect.

R356 Lane 2c — the auth/legal/404 sheets' PAPER GRAIN FILM (patterns.css:686, the r314 recipe: feTurbulence data-URI + 24px micro-dot grid, mix-blend-mode multiply, z-index 0, pointer-events none): a static decorative TEXTURE under the flowing content — the same proven-intentional fixed-decor family as div.sheet-frame / div.auth-frame (allowlisted R313/R353). inset:0 BY CONSTRUCTION (it is the paper's grain, not a cover); it paints texture, never ink or controls, and reduced-motion has nothing to collapse (static). Surfaced by the Lane 2c crawl only as a lazy-mount race on one 404-rendering path (the same page crawled clean when the chunk landed earlier) — allowlisting the film, not hiding a defect: text-on-text/clipped/overflow findings are never filtered.
